cases.statement: Three carriers in two unrelated reports: a Korean infant and her affected father (32743991), and patient 5 of a French paediatric cohort (41741169).

people.label: patient (proband infant)
people.key_phenotypes: infantile-onset recurrent fever; erythematous rash (biopsy suggesting panniculitis); oral ulcers; elevated liver enzymes; fluctuating autoantibodies (ANA, anti-dsDNA, anti-Ro)

quotes.quote: A 2-month-old infant exhibited symptoms including recurrent fever, erythematous rashes, and oral ulcers, with elevated liver enzymes, and tested positive for several autoantibodies
heterozygous nonsense variation of the TNFAIP3 gene was considered as the prime candidate; NM_006290.3:c.492G>A (p.Trp164Ter)
A skin biopsy was performed, which demonstrated multifocal histiocytic infiltration, mainly in the perivascular and periappendiceal areas in the dermis and subcutis suggesting panniculitis.
Our patient also had fluctuating low autoantibodies from early infancy.

people.label: father of patient
people.zygosity_or_genotype: carrier (zygosity not stated; the proband's variant was inherited from him)
people.key_phenotypes: recurrent oral and genital ulcers, knee arthralgia, abdominal pain and diarrhea since his teens (Behçet-like)

quotes.quote: Reexamination of detailed family history revealed that her father had recurrent symptoms, including oral and genital ulcers, knee arthralgia, abdominal pain, and diarrhea.
These Behçet-like symptoms have lasted for many years, since he was a teenager
The c.492G>A variation of the proband was inherited from her father.

people.label: Patient 5 (family 3)
people.key_phenotypes: onset age 3 y; fever; abdominal pain and diarrhoea; ulcerated colitis with atypical features; necrotic finger lesions; lymphadenopathy (pedigree)

phenotype_specificity.statement: In 32743991 the infant was first thought to have neonatal lupus; maternal autoantibodies were negative, and exome sequencing also found an NF1 variant that the authors link to her café-au-lait spots. The authors say her picture so far looks more like an early-onset periodic fever syndrome than typical Behçet disease. The father's features are Behçet-like. In 41741169, patient 5 had colitis, fever and skin lesions. The cohort was tested with autoinflammatory gene panels (cohort-level statement), and no other genes are named for this patient.

quotes.quote: Several laboratory tests were performed to identify autoantibodies in the mother; these were all negative.

Additionally, WES revealed another known pathogenic mutation in the NF1 gene (c.4103T>G, p.Leu1368*, heterozygote), causing neurofibromatosis, which was evident due to the presence of multiple café au lait spots.
So far, her symptoms are like early-onset periodic fever syndrome than typical Behçet syndrome.
the infant's and her father's symptoms point towards an autoinflammatory syndrome called autosomal dominant Behçet's disease
In 16 out of 17 patients, a next-generation sequencing (NGS) panel for autoinflammatory diseases was performed.

segregation.statement: 32743991: one affected relative (the father, Behçet-like features) carries the variant, confirmed by Sanger sequencing. A grandmother had an ankylosing-spondylitis-like disease but was not tested. The mother's genotype is not reported. 41741169: family history is recorded as 'Absent' for P5. Segregation data for this person are not reported.

quotes.quote: The variant was confirmed by Sanger sequencing in the infant and her father.
The c.492G>A variation of the proband was inherited from her father.
Her grandmother also had suffered from long-standing ankylosing spondylitis-like disease, although we could not check the details of the disease.

de_novo.statement: Not de novo in 32743991: inherited from the affected father. For 41741169 patient 5, parental testing is not reported for this person. The paper says three patients were the only family members tested, but it does not name them (cohort-level).

quotes.quote: The c.492G>A variation of the proband was inherited from her father.
The remaining three patients were the only family members who underwent genetic testing, as their relatives were asymptomatic.

functional.statement: No functional assay of this variant. 32743991 states that the authors considered a functional study unnecessary.

quotes.quote: so we believe that no additional functional study is necessary to confirm its pathogenicity

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Nonsense variant (c.492G>A, p.(Trp164Ter)), located in the OTU domain according to 41741169. Both papers describe the disease as caused by loss-of-function variants (haploinsufficiency).

quotes.quote: Haploinsufficiency of A20 (HA20) is a newly described autoinflammatory disease caused by loss-of-function mutations in the TNFAIP3 gene.
considering that it is a nonsense mutation leading to early termination of the protein A20 and a truncated protein during translation
A20 haploinsufficiency (HA20) is a monogenic, early-onset autoinflammatory disease caused by loss-of-function variants in the tumour necrosis factor alpha-induced protein 3 (TNFAIP3) gene

computational_predictions.statement: 32743991 reports a MutationTaster prediction and conservation scores.

quotes.quote: pathogenic predictions by MutationTaster revealed a pathogenic effect
The DNA position appeared to be conserved across species (GERP++gt2 6.08; phyloP20way_mammalian 1.048; phastCons20way_mammalian 0.999).

population_data_in_papers.statement: 32743991: absent from the population databases searched (EVS, ExAC, gnomAD, KRGDB were the databases named in the methods).

quotes.quote: This variation was neither found in population databases nor reported as a pathogenic variant in the literature or databases.
Exome Aggregation Consortium (http://exac.broadinstitute.org/), gnomAD (http://gnomad.broadinstitute.org/)

authors_classification.statement: 32743991 uses two different wordings (case section and discussion); 41741169 Table 3 gives its own classification. All three are quoted.

quotes.quote: it is a definite pathogenic mutation
WES revealed likely pathogenic variant nonsense mutations in the TNFAIP3 gene leading to HA20

concerns: The 32743991 proband also carries a heterozygous NF1 nonsense variant (c.4103T>G, p.Leu1368*). The authors attribute her café-au-lait spots to it.
32743991 is inconsistent about its own classification: the case section and the discussion use different wordings (both quoted under authors_classification).
Papers use NM_006290.3 (32743991) and NM_006290.4 (41741169), not the batch transcript NM_001270508.2. The cDNA and protein positions agree with the batch record.
41741169 Table 3 cites references 12 and 21 for this variant, so it may have been published before. The reference list is not in the text file, so the cited reports could not be identified.
The two reports look like different people: Korean infant with an affected father vs a French-cohort girl (P5) with family history 'Absent', onset age 3 y and diagnosis at 9 y.
41741169 gives no zygosity or parental testing for patient 5 individually.
notes_for_panel: Father (HA20-ID0088) is an affected carrier, which counts as one informative segregation. Nothing is reported on functional studies of this variant.
